tasks.name: @compmd/render: the renderer package
tasks.description:
Create `@compmd/render` in `render/` (TypeScript, standalone, never refers to any application) with the three layers of the processor's design, as an earlier prototype shaped them. Start clean from spec §7.4 to §7.6 and §9 with what the earlier prototypes learned; no spike code.

## Layers

- **Component:** one component node into a target, with its box, its binding, and slots and a fallback the caller renders; `update` and `destroy`.
- **Region:** any subtree, components through the component layer, updated in place by key; it takes the inputs, the last heading level before it, the footnotes numbered so far and a place in the page's container.
- **Page:** the region at the root, plus the container breakpoints query, the theme tokens as `--compmd-*` custom properties, footnote numbering and the inputs; one stylesheet per document.

## Keys

Keys from origins (spec §12.3) by the processor's design's mapping rule, with the edit's range from the caller and a diff only for merged changes.

## Invalid text

The rules for invalid text (the processor's design):

- the last good page for broken frontmatter;
- an unclosed top-level container's opener as a paragraph;
- the last good render of a top-level block with any other error.

## Rendering

- Markdown.
- `box` with its layout and common params as CSS.
- Host-language components through the host contract (spec §7.4) with every slot rendered up front.
- The React, Svelte 5 and plain bindings (spec §7.6).
- The reference rendering of the built-ins (spec §13.1, informative).

It renders inside a frame the caller supplies (the editor a sandboxed iframe, the app its sandbox), with a small host and frame protocol.

## Tests

Tests from an earlier prototype's cases:

- the identity matrix (every component and its state through the charter's edits);
- the four invalid-text cases;
- the page layer against the region layer.

Unit tests in a DOM.

tasks.name: Spec: layout rules from the @compmd/render review
tasks.description:
Write into the CompMD spec the layout rules settled with the user in the review of CMD-48's `@compmd/render` (2026-10-27). The spec never refers to any application.

## Decided

1. **Breakpoints follow the nearest box** (§9.3). Replace "its parent's width" with the width of its *nearest box*, the term §9.2 already uses for positions. List items, quotes and alerts don't count, so a component in a list item inside a box follows the box.
2. **A component follows its nearest box, not its own width** (§9.3), and this is intended. Add the example: a `card` fenced `{padding=s md:padding=m}` in `::: grid {min=14rem}` on a 1000 px page gets `m` in every card, since the grid is 1000 px wide, though each card is about 320 px.
3. **W114 for every block whose width comes from its content** (§9.3, §10.2). This is a block whose children use breakpoints that is:
   - in a `row` (as now);
   - positioned (`inset-*`) without a `width`;
   - or has `align-self` or `justify-self` other than `stretch`.

   Without a `width`, such a block shrinks to nothing.
4. **A note in §7.4.** A host-language component that lays its slot items out by their content (a toolbar row) gives each item a width when its blocks use breakpoints. A processor can't check this.
5. **A glossary, §1.1 *Terms*.** One line per term, each with a link to its section:
   - *processor*, *plain renderer*, *component* and *built-in* (moved from §1);
   - *host language*, *binding*, *host contract*, *pack*;
   - *box* and *outer box*, *nearest box*, *item*;
   - *slot* and *template slot*, *fallback*, *input*;
   - *parse tree* and *expanded tree*, *origin*, *breakpoint*.

   "Container" then means only a `:::` component (§4.1). §9.3's "is the container they follow" becomes "is the box they follow"; *query container* stays the CSS mechanism, named only in the renderer's README. The two entries settled in the review:

   > **Box.** The rectangle a block is laid out in. Every component invocation that is a block has one *outer box* (section 9.2): a host-language component's `target`, or the box holding a `compmd` component's body. A `display=contents` component has none.
   >
   > **Nearest box** (of a block). The closest box around it in the expanded tree (section 12.3): a `box` (a `compmd` component's box among them), a host-language component's outer box, or one item of a host-language component's slot. List items, quotes, table cells, `each`, `if`, the slots of `compmd` components and `display=contents` components don't count. At the top level, it is the area the processor renders into. A positioned block is placed in its nearest box (section 9.2), and its breakpoints follow its nearest box's width (section 9.3).

The region outside a page was settled in the same review and is done in CMD-48: the caller provides the box.

## Also

- Add conformance cases for each rule and each W114 variant. Re-record the expected trees with a processor, as the W114 change of 2026-10-24 did.
- Add a short informative part of §9 with the examples from the review: top level, a narrow box, own params only, the card grid, a list item, `display=contents`, a host component's slot, and `each`/`if`.
- Add a CHANGELOG entry naming the sections, and update `llms.txt` where it states these rules.

tasks.name: Claim the compmd crate on crates.io (needs the user)
tasks.description:
Claim the name `compmd` on crates.io by publishing the placeholder crate. crates.io has no way to reserve a name without publishing. The user does it, since it needs their account.

## Steps

1. On crates.io (signed in with GitHub), add and verify an email address in the account settings; publishing needs it. On 2026-10-27 this failed with *Too Many Requests*, to be tried again.
2. Create an API token that can publish new crates, and run `cargo login` with it.
3. Publish: `cargo publish --manifest-path processor/Cargo.toml`. The `compmd` commit with the crate is pushed first, so the published crate matches the repository.
4. Optionally, add the `comp-markdown` GitHub organization as an owner (`cargo owner --add github:comp-markdown:<team>`), so the crate isn't tied to one account.

## Also

- **npm:** the `compmd` organization holds the `@compmd` scope. Turn on two-factor authentication for the account and require it for the organization. Scoped packages publish as private by default, so `@compmd/render` needs `"publishConfig": { "access": "public" }` before its first release.

Version `0.0.1` can't be published again, so the first real release is `0.1.0` or later.

tasks.name: Spec: Pandoc's math rule in full; code spans in fallbacks
tasks.description:
Two corrections to spec §2.3 and §4, settled with the user after an earlier prototype's parser. The spec never refers to any application.

## Decided

1. **Inline math follows Pandoc's rule in full (§2.3).** The spec's summary misses a clause, and the prototype and an earlier prototype's spike follow the summary. The missing clause: inside the math, outside a `{…}` group, an unescaped `$` with white space (a space, tab or line break) on its left ends the attempt, and the opening `$` is text. Checked with Pandoc 3.12.1:
   - `It costs $5 and $6. Math $x^2$ here.`: `$5` and `$6.` are text, `$x^2$` is math (the summary made `5 and $6. Math $x^2` one span).
   - `Money then math: $20 and $x$ and $30.`: only `$x$` is math.
   - `Three: $a $b$ c`: `$a` is text, `$b$` is math.
   - `$x{y $ z}$ w`: math `x{y $ z}`; inside a group, a `$` after a space is content.
   - `$a \$ b$ c`: math `a \$ b`.
   - A line break counts as white space: `$a` then a new line with `$b$ c` gives text `$a`, math `b`.
2. **Code spans bind tighter than an inline component's or leaf's brackets (§4.3, §4.4),** as in CommonMark's link text: a `]` inside a code span doesn't end the fallback. `:a[b `c]` d]` has the fallback `` b `c]` d `` with the code span `c]`, as a plain renderer shows it. A run of backticks counts as a code span only when a run of the same length closes it; otherwise the backticks are text.

## Also

- Conformance cases: the Pandoc outputs above for math (Pandoc is the reference), and a fallback with `]` in a code span, inline and on a leaf line.
- The prototype (`spikes/markdown-flavor/`): both rules, so its conformance run stays green.
- an earlier prototype's spike (`spikes/compmd-rust/`): both rules in the fork's constructs, its patch regenerated, and `hard_cases.rs`'s math test corrected.
- A CHANGELOG entry naming the sections (breaking for documents that relied on the old reading), and `llms.txt` where it states these rules.

tasks.name: [A.3] Decide whether cel and md stay public
tasks.description:
Hosts don't use `cel` or `md` directly. Today their only outside users are four test files (1,814 lines) and the doc examples:

- `cel_profile.rs` (466 lines), `cel_errors.rs` (654), `md_functions.rs` (353);
- `differential.rs` (341), which checks the profile against the `cel` crate, a dev-dependency.

Their public surface:
- `cel`: `Program`, `Scope`, `Values`, `Type`, `Value`, `Key`, `Error`, `BUDGET`, `MAX_DEPTH`, and the `FunctionTypes` and `Functions` traits.
- `md`: `Md` and `Signatures`.

What they depend on in the crate:
- `cel` uses `tree::DeclaredType`, `named` and `nearest`.
- `md` uses `cel`, `host::Time` and ICU4X.

**Needs the user's decision before work starts.** There are three options.

## Option 1: keep them public, as a documented sub-API

They stay `compmd::cel` and `compmd::md`, with the README section and the doc examples.

- **For:**
  - A tool that checks or evaluates one expression can use them without a document: an editor's hover and type errors, or a host formatting a value the way `md.date` does.
  - No code moves.
- **Against:**
  - Every type above is public API, so semver binds them and their docs must be kept up.
  - `Md::new(now, lang, tz, time)` repeats what `Context` already holds, which is a second way in.
  - No such tool exists yet.
- **Work:** small. Review the docs and the surface, and decide whether `Md::new` stays.

## Option 2: make them crate-private, and move the tests to unit tests

`pub mod cel` and `pub mod md` become `mod`, and `lib.rs` re-exports nothing from them.

- **For:**
  - The public API is only what a host uses: `Processor`, `host`, `context`, `expand`, `expanded`, `tree`, `diagnostic`, `process`, `Ambient`, `ParseOptions`.
  - Internals can change freely.
- **Against:**
  - The tests move: they become `#[cfg(test)]` modules, such as `cel/tests/profile.rs`, `cel/tests/errors.rs`, `cel/tests/differential.rs` and `md/tests/functions.rs`. Mostly the imports change, and the dev-dependency `cel` still works there.
  - The doc examples in `cel.rs`, `cel/types.rs` and `cel/value.rs` stop running as doctests, so they become unit tests or go.
  - The README's CEL section goes.
- **Work:** medium, and mechanical. No behaviour changes.

## Option 3: a separate crate, `compmd-cel`, in the workspace

The CEL profile (parser, checker, evaluator, and the `FunctionTypes` and `Functions` traits) becomes its own crate, public by being one. `compmd` depends on it, and `md` stays in `compmd`, crate-private.

- **For:**
  - A reusable CEL-profile crate, which tools can depend on without the processor and without ICU4X.
  - `compmd`'s API stays small.
  - A crate boundary keeps the profile independent of the processor.
- **Against:**
  - The three dependencies have to move or be inverted. `DeclaredType` to `Type` becomes a conversion in `compmd`, and `named` and `nearest` move to the new crate or are duplicated.
  - One more crate to publish, version and document, alongside `compmd` and `compmd-markdown`.
  - `md_functions.rs` becomes unit tests in `compmd`, as in option 2.
- **Work:** the largest.

## Recommendation

Option 2. Nothing outside uses the modules, so keeping them public only adds API to maintain (YAGNI). If a tool such as an editor's language server needs expressions on their own later, option 3 is the way to open them up then, and option 2 is a step towards it.

CI green, 99.34% lines.
Approved in review with no comments; compmd `1019a2c` (option 2). Option 3, a `compmd-cel` crate, is for when a tool needs expressions on their own.

tasks.name: [A.4] Decide where the JSON request lives
tasks.description:
## Decision

The `Processor` is `compmd`'s only way in. The `process` module goes, with no one-call wrapper left in its place. The JSON request format moves to `compmd-wasm`, its one user (the CompMD editor, later).

## Changes

### `compmd`
- **Remove `process`:** `Request`, `Packs`, `Pack`, `Remote`, `HostData`, `Processed`, `Needed`, `Error`, `process()`, `sources()`, and `From<Processor<Expanded>> for Processed` in `processor.rs`.
- **In-memory hosts in `host`**, next to `Files for HashMap<String, String>`:
  - `Fetch for HashMap<String, Fetched>`;
  - `Data for HashMap<String, Json>`;
  - `Packs for HashMap<String, Vec<Pack>>`, with a new public `host::Pack { version, integrity, files }` (`Deserialize`, like `Fetched`).
- **The render time from text:** the crate-private RFC 3339 parser (`cel::time::parse_timestamp`) gets a public, documented entry in `context`, giving the nanoseconds `Context::now` takes.
- **Docs:** the crate docs and README describe the `Processor` chain only.

### `compmd-wasm`
- Its own request module holds the JSON `Request` (same fields, `camelCase`), so the TypeScript API is unchanged.
- `process` runs the chain from `new` to `expand` and serializes `{parse, expanded, diagnostics}` from `tree()`, `expanded()` and `diagnostics()`.
- `sources` runs the chain to `validate` and maps the sources to `{remote, host}`.
- A request whose document isn't one of its files is an error, as before.
- **Coverage:** check whether the crate builds natively despite its `wasm-bindgen` import. If it does, give the request module native unit tests and bring the crate into the coverage gate; if not, say so, and the TypeScript tests stay its only cover.

### Conformance runner (`processor/tests/conformance.rs`)
- Builds the typed parts from the case folder: files, packs, remote and host data as the `host` maps, `Ambient`, allowed origins, a `Context` (with `now` through the public parser, `Zones` as `time`), and `expand::Options`.
- Runs the chain itself, with no JSON round trip, and reads `diagnostics()` and `expanded()`.

### `resolve.rs` unit tests
- Use `HashMap<String, Vec<host::Pack>>` in place of `process::Packs`.

### Not changed
- No application uses `compmd` yet. `@compmd/render` and the preview spike don't use the crate.
- `Source` and the list of what to fetch are CMD-65. The hand-kept TypeScript `Request` type stays as it is.

## Options considered

1. Keep `process` in `compmd`: the JSON format stays `compmd` API, and there are two ways in.
2. Move it into `compmd-wasm` (chosen, with the shared in-memory hosts and the public time parser).
3. A separate `compmd-json` crate: one more crate for about 300 lines.

tasks.name: [A.5] One type for what to fetch
tasks.description:
## Decision

Option 1: `Processor::sources` returns `host::Needed { remote, host }`, and `load::Source` goes.
- Each URL and each `host:` source is listed once, at its first place.
- The fields keep the names `remote` and `host`.
- The test hosts are replaced in CMD-81, after this task.

## The issue

A host that fetches before it loads asks the validated processor what a render needs: `Processor::sources(&context)`. Three types now describe the same list:

- **`load::Source`** (public): `Remote(url)` or `Host(source)`, which `Processor::sources` returns as one `Vec`, in the order they are written. It is the only public item of `load`, so `load` is a public module for one enum.
- **`Needed { remote, host }`** in `compmd-wasm` (`wasm/src/request.rs`): since CMD-64 it lives only there, as what `sources` gives in JSON. The binding loops over the `Vec<Source>` to split it into the two lists. The TypeScript `Needed` type in `wasm/src/index.ts` mirrors it.
- **`from::Target`** (internal to `load`): `Remote`, `Host` or `File`. `load::sources` maps two of its variants to `Source` and drops `File`.

Also relevant:
- The name `Source` is also `resolve::source::Source`, the internal kind of an *import* source (a pack, a relative path…), so the same word means two things in the crate.
- Repeated sources aren't merged. A URL written in two data imports is listed twice, and the host fetches it twice unless it removes duplicates itself.
- The only users of the list are `compmd-wasm` (`request.rs`) and one test in `tests/expand.rs` (`data_comes_from_packs_urls_and_hosts`). Nobody uses the order across the two kinds, only the order within each.
- The spec says nothing about this list. It is processor API only.

## Options

1. **One struct, `host::Needed { remote, host }`.**
   - `Processor::sources` returns it. It sits in `host` beside `Fetch` and `Data`, since it says what those will be asked for, and derives `Serialize`.
   - `load::Source` goes, and with it `load`'s only public item, so `load` becomes a private module.
   - `compmd-wasm` serializes it as it is, so its own `Needed` and the loop go.
   - Loses: the order across the two kinds, which nobody uses.
2. **Keep the enum, in a better place.**
   - Move `Source` to `host` under a name that doesn't clash, and make `load` private.
   - `compmd-wasm` keeps its `Needed` and the loop.
   - Loses nothing, but the binding keeps a second type for the same list.
3. **As it is:** only the name clash and the public `load` module would be fixed elsewhere, if at all.

**Recommendation:** option 1. One type says it, in the module where the host already looks.

## Open questions

- **Duplicates:** should the list name each URL and each `host:` source once, at its first place? I recommend yes: a host never wants to fetch the same URL twice for one render.
- **Field names:** `remote` and `host` match the JSON and TypeScript today. Keep them? I recommend yes.

## Changes, if option 1

- `processor/src/host.rs`: `Needed`, with docs and a unit test.
- `processor/src/load.rs`: `sources` builds `Needed`; `Source` removed.
- `processor/src/lib.rs`: `mod load;` (private). Check that nothing public names a `load` item.
- `processor/src/processor.rs`: `sources` returns `Needed`.
- `wasm/src/request.rs`: serialize `Needed` from `compmd`; its own `Needed` and the loop go.
- `processor/tests/expand.rs`: assert on `Needed`.
- Docs: the `load` module docs and the README's line on `sources`.

Related: `tests/expand.rs` and `tests/stages.rs` still have their own test hosts (`Kit`, `Web`, `Host`, `Packs`), which the `host` map implementations from CMD-64 could replace (CMD-81).

New test `each_source_is_needed_once_at_its_first_place`. CI green (99.34% lines), wasm tests pass.

tasks.name: Report type names outside the spec's grammar
tasks.description:
## The issue

A declaration's type is one of the spec's type names (§7.3 grammar: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `array`, `object`, `length`, `space`, `color`, `tracks`, `surface`, `border`, `radius`, `name`, an enum, or `input<type>`). A name outside that list, such as a typo (`numbr`, `strng`), is accepted silently today:

- The processor keeps it as `DeclaredType::Other`, written as is in the tree.
- Since CMD-73 it fits any value everywhere, as `dyn`: a param of that type takes any value, an expression of it checks as `dyn`, a data `schema` field takes any cell, and an input of it takes any given value.
- Nothing reports it. An author who writes `count: numbr` gets no type checking and no hint.

The spec has no diagnostic for it: the diagnostics table (§10) has nothing for a type name outside the grammar.

## Decide first (spec)

1. **The code:** a new F code (an error, like F009 for a value outside its type), or a W code (a warning, the declaration still works as `dyn`)? Or does an existing code fit: F009 is about values, F013 about names.
2. **What the declaration then is:** refused (the param treated as undeclared, so F008 at each use?), or kept as `dyn` with the diagnostic only?
3. **Where it is reported:** the declaration in a signature, an input or a data `schema`, at the type's position, with the nearest type name as a hint (`numbr` → "did you mean `number`?").
4. **Where it is checked:** stage 2 (resolve, with the signatures and settings) or stage 3 (validate).

Settle these with the user, then write the spec change (the diagnostics table and §7.3) and a conformance case, before the processor change.

## Then

- The processor reports it, with the hint from `nearest`.
- Tests: a conformance case for each place (signature, input, schema).

notes.text: Decided with the user: **F037**, an error; the declaration is kept as `dyn`; reported at the type name (short form, long form `type`, inside `input<…>`), with the nearest type name and a fix; checked in stage 2 (resolve).

F037 (spec §7.3, §10.2, changelog), CompMD `d0e9e7b`. At the type name (quotes, indented fences, inside `input<…>`; bare `enum` counts), nearest name + fix, stage 2; kept as `dyn`. 3 conformance cases (177), message tests, an edit-test paste; `llms.txt` and counts updated. `cargo make ci` green.
Approved in review. F037: CompMD `d0e9e7b`.

tasks.name: Fork: unclosed frontmatter breaks later lines
tasks.description:
Fix a bug in the markdown-rs fork (`markdown-rs/`, branch `compmd`): with the `frontmatter` construct on, a first `---` line that is never closed makes the fork parse the lines after it wrongly.

## Repro

`---\nus\n- a\n` with `Constructs { frontmatter: true, ..Constructs::default() }` gives a thematic break and the paragraph `us\n- a`; with the construct off (and per CommonMark) it is a thematic break, the paragraph `us` and a list. Plain CommonMark constructs reproduce it, so the bug is upstream's.

## Found so far

- The list item construct is never even attempted on line 3: neither `list_item::start` nor `document::container_new_before`/`container_existing_before` run for lines 2 and later with the construct on.
- So the failed frontmatter attempt (it scans to the end of the text, then fails in `content_end`) leaves the document tokenizer in a state where later lines don't go through the container checks. Look at what the attempt's revert restores and what it doesn't (`document_child`, line starts, `tokenize_state`).

## Do

- Find the cause and fix it in the fork, the smallest change that makes the construct's failure leave no trace.
- Test in `tests/frontmatter.rs`: the repro and variants (blank lines, lists, block quotes, fences after the unclosed `---`) parse the same with the construct on and off.
- The fork's full test suite passes (`cargo test --all-features`).
- In compmd, the processor works around it (`Syntax::mdast` turns the construct on only for closed frontmatter, and `incremental.md` says so under *Found while designing*). Once fixed, decide with the user whether to keep the workaround; update the note.

Push order: fork, then compmd.

tasks.name: Components from apps and packs: a design (security, speed and size, experience)
tasks.description:
Asked by the user (2026-10-30), from the website's "Use it in your app" snippets (CMD-103): how does an application give documents components of its own, written in React or Svelte and compiled with the app? And, settled with the user the same day, how a pack ships code at all, which the Mermaid pack (CMD-115) follows.

**The gap.** Today a document can name a component only if it is defined: locally, in an imported file, or in a pack (spec §6.3). Packs are npm packages already (§6.4). An app that ships its own `Stars` React component must still put it in an ambient pack *with a `jsx` fence holding its code* (a signature fence alone is F002: nothing to attach to), and then mount its own compiled version through the renderer's `components` map. The code in the fence is never run.

**The deliverable: a design document** in `docs/`, reviewed with the user before any spec or code change, with:

- **The alternatives**, each with a concrete example from the app's side, the pack author's side and the document's side. For example:
  - a *host-provided* definition: a signature with no code, which the host promises to implement;
  - an ambient pack published on npm with the compiled component;
  - the current way.
- **Worked examples:** an app's own `Stars` (React) and `Rating` (Svelte); a shared pack of charts; the Mermaid pack of CMD-115 (a large third-party library).
- **The analysis of each alternative:**
  - **Security** (spec §15): who supplies code and who runs it; whether an app's own components run outside the sandbox, and what a document can make them do through params and slots; whether an npm pack could pretend to be a host component, or the reverse; supply chain (versions, integrity, scopes; `@compmd/*` is reserved); how `componentsOf`, fallbacks and W113 report such names.
  - **Speed and size:** what loads, when, and how much (Mermaid's size as the hard case); compiling in the browser against shipping built code; caching across documents.
  - **Author and user experience:** writing a component, sharing it, reusing it in other documents and apps, versions and updates, what a plain renderer and another processor show (fallbacks, F002), and how a document states what it depends on.
- **What changes where:** the spec (§6, §7, §15), the processor, `@compmd/processor`'s request, `@compmd/render`'s `components`, the playground, the conformance set.
- **A recommendation**, and what it means for CMD-115 and for the website's third snippet.

Finding: a host component as a signature alone in an ambient pack already works (checked with 0.1.1: validation, W113, `componentLeaf`). Proposes B for apps (`hostPack` helper, spec wording in §6.3, §7.1, §15) and D for large packs (built modules by URL; Mermaid 976 KB gz).

tasks.name: Website: move it to compmd.hakanserce.com (Route 53, GitHub Pages)
tasks.description:
Move the CompMD website from `comp-markdown.github.io/compmd/` to **`compmd.hakanserce.com`** (`website/docs/design.md` decision 3). `hakanserce.com` is on AWS Route 53. Done by the user, in this order; then an agent checks the site at its new address.

**1. Verify the domain for the `comp-markdown` organization** first, so no one else's GitHub Pages can claim it.
- GitHub: `github.com/organizations/comp-markdown/settings/pages` → **Add a domain** → `compmd.hakanserce.com`.
- GitHub shows a TXT record to add: a name like `_github-pages-challenge-comp-markdown.compmd.hakanserce.com` and a value (a code).
- Route 53: **Hosted zones** → `hakanserce.com` → **Create record**:
  - Record name: `_github-pages-challenge-comp-markdown.compmd` (Route 53 adds `.hakanserce.com`)
  - Type: `TXT`
  - Value: the code, in double quotes
  - TTL: `300`
- Back on GitHub, **Verify**. It can take a few minutes for the record to be seen; the TXT record must stay.

**2. Point the subdomain at GitHub Pages.** Route 53, the same hosted zone, **Create record**:
- Record name: `compmd`
- Type: `CNAME` (a plain record, not an alias)
- Value: `comp-markdown.github.io` (no `/compmd`; GitHub finds the repository from the domain)
- TTL: `300`

If the zone has a `CAA` record, it must allow GitHub's certificate authority: add `0 issue "letsencrypt.org"` to it. Without any `CAA` record, nothing is needed.

**3. Set the custom domain on the repository.**
- GitHub: `github.com/comp-markdown/compmd/settings/pages` → **Custom domain** → `compmd.hakanserce.com` → **Save**.
- Wait for the DNS check to pass and the certificate to be issued (minutes, up to an hour or so), then tick **Enforce HTTPS**.

tasks.name: Packs from a registry at run time (design)
tasks.description:
Re-scoped with the user (2026-10-31): S3 as first written (a pack's libraries resolved by the host) is deferred. What the user wants is **documents that use packs straight from a registry, at run time**: a host gives its documents one or more registries, `@compmd/processor` (or a package next to it) provides a `Registry` interface and an `NpmRegistry` implementation, and a host that is fine with it lets documents import any pack from it. This builds the accepted design's **H2** (configuration filled from the registry at run time) and **P2** (any npm pack, in the strict sandbox) in `docs/components-from-apps-and-packs.md`, which were decided but never built: today only H3 (packs installed at build time, `@compmd/vite`) and folder packs exist, so an import of a pack the host didn't install is F026.

**First a design doc**, reviewed with the user before any code, since its points are coupled and touch security. Say what the spec already settles and only decide what it doesn't. §6.4 already settles: `@scope/pack` is the npm package of that name, from npm or a registry the processor is configured with (a mirror, a private one); the `compmd` field of `package.json` names the pack's document (default `index.comp.md`); `package.json` is the manifest `export.pack` and `export.version` must match; an import's `integrity` is the hash the registry publishes; `@compmd/*` is reserved; names are scoped; a size cap is allowed; built modules load by their place in the pack; "the processor gets packs, never the reader's browser" (privacy).

**To decide, with alternatives and a recommendation each:**

1. **Privacy against hosts with no server.** §6.4 and §15 forbid the reader's browser fetching from the registry; a static host (the playground on GitHub Pages) has nothing else. A proxy or cache the host runs, a host opting in to direct fetching with what that discloses, a CDN mirror; and whether the spec's rule needs refining.
2. **The sandbox's origin.** Strict frames load scripts only from the host's origin (`docs/sandbox.md`); a registry pack's built module comes from elsewhere. The host serves it (proxy, or a `blob:` module checked against integrity), or the frame's policy admits the registry's origin.
3. **Integrity.** npm's `dist.integrity` covers the tarball: fetch and unpack it (gzip, tar) and check it, or trust a file CDN's per-file hashes.
4. **The API.** `process()` is synchronous and takes packs in the request; registry packs need an async resolver before it: read the imports, resolve ranges against the registry's versions, fetch, follow each pack's own imports, then process; caching, and the editor processing again on every edit. Where it lives (`@compmd/processor`, a new package) and how it fits `@compmd/vite`'s configuration (`compmd.config.json`: registries, `imports`, `deny`, size cap).
5. **Several registries.** Which one serves a scope (per scope, as `.npmrc` does), and what a document may name versus what the host gives.
6. **Conventions for CompMD packs on npm** beyond §6.4: a keyword (for example `compmd-pack`) for discovery, what a pack's tarball must hold, the size cap's default, caching and offline use.
7. **What changes:** the spec (if any rule needs refining), the processor, `@compmd/sandbox`, `@compmd/vite`, the playground (documents importing published packs), docs; and the implementation tasks to add after the design is accepted.

**Related:** CMD-137 (the spec's rules for what a component's imports resolve to) should settle first or alongside, so registry packs follow a spec that matches the code. CMD-115 (the Mermaid pack) is the first real pack on npm, a natural end-to-end test.

**The gaps, with where they are:**

1. **Runtimes in built modules.** §6.4 *Built modules* says a built module has "the libraries it uses bundled in". 4. **To settle with the user:** whether a pack may name the libraries it expects from the host (for example as `peerDependencies`), so a host can report a missing one up front instead of at render.

tasks.name: Create-pack: registry conventions and a library-pack template
tasks.description:
From CMD-131's accepted design (`docs/packs-from-a-registry.md`, R6, R9) and the companion `compmd-registry-v1.md`, sections 2 and 5. Already in the template: the `compmd` field, the keyword `compmd-pack`, and `files`.

## Pack template
- **One file per module.** The library-mode build turns off code splitting, so a library that loads parts of itself on demand stays in `dist/<component>.js`. A test checks there are no relative or dynamic imports of chunks.
- **Shared libraries are peers.** The build leaves out every name in `peerDependencies`, not only the runtimes.
- **README:** how to use a library pack: `npm install -D @kit/three`, add `"@kit/three": "^0.170"` to `peerDependencies`, import it by that name, and list it in `demo/compmd.config.json` under `libraries` so the test page offers it (`@compmd/vite` shares libraries only as ones it offers, L1).

## Library-pack template
`npm create @compmd/pack three -- --library three` writes `@<user>/three`:
- `src/index.ts` re-exports the npm package `three`. It is built as one ES module, `dist/index.js`, whose only imports are runtimes and other libraries named in `peerDependencies`.
- `package.json` has `"compmd": { "library": "dist/index.js" }`, `exports` for the same file, the keyword `compmd-pack`, `files: ["dist", "README.md"]`, and the wrapped package as a dev dependency.
- **Its version is the library's.** The build sets `version` to the installed library's version, with a warning, as it writes `peerDependencies`. `prepublishOnly` checks that they match.
- It has no document, no components and no test page. Its README says when to add `"single": true` (a library that can't have two copies in one sandbox), and there is no flag for it.
- `--library` refuses `--renders` and `--component`.

## Docs and tests
- `docs/create-pack.md` gets the decisions above. The create-pack README and the template READMEs are updated.
- **Tests:**
  - `createPack` with `--library`: the files written and the fields.
  - A generated library pack built from the workspace: one module file, `version` equal to the library's, and the `compmd` field.
  - A generated pack built with a library in `peerDependencies`: the library is left out of `dist/`.

markdown-rs's tokenizer skips lines after a failed attempt that crossed line endings: it recorded each line's start one index early, which nothing read until such an attempt left entries behind. With the frontmatter construct on, `---\nus\n- a\n` (a first `---` never closed) parses `- a` into the paragraph `us`, where CommonMark makes it a list, as it does with the construct off. Found by the incremental parser's differential test; fixed in the fork (`compmd-markdown`) in commit `79f6e2e`, checked by `tests/frontmatter.rs` there.

## Steps

1. Check the bug is still in markdown-rs's latest release.
2. Draft an issue and a pull request from the fork's fix and its test, without the fork's CompMD constructs.
3. The user opens them on GitHub, since they go out under their account.

Once merged upstream, the fork picks the fix up with its next rebase.

Approved: Drafts approved in review. Left: push the branch for the PR (with the user’s go), the user opens the issue and the PR, then record their links.

Check the posts, then done.

tasks.name: Handling pack loading states (loading, loaded, failed)
tasks.description:
Found in CMD-131's design review (user, 2026-10-31): the spec has no state for an import that is still on its way. Everything loads in stage 4a, before evaluation (§11), so a pack is there or F026. With packs from a registry at run time (`docs/packs-from-a-registry.md`), a processor renders before a pack arrives. The user wants *package load pending* information as well as *not loaded* and *loaded* events, designed on its own: it may change the processor, the renderer, the sandbox and the editor.

**First a design doc**, reviewed: fill in the placeholder `docs/handling-pack-loading-states.md`, which lists what to settle: the three states, what a reader sees, what a host and a component learn, diagnostics, and late data. Then the spec change (§4.5, §8.5, §11, §12.3) and the implementation tasks.

Until then, `docs/packs-from-a-registry.md` (decision 7) uses the spec as it is: while a pack loads, its uses show their fallback text, and the document renders again when it arrives.

## Also in scope (2026-11-02)
- **The playground shows it today:** its `?doc=npm` document lists F026 for `@comp-markdown/mermaid` while the pack is fetched, as if it didn't exist (CMD-146).
- **A component that recovers:** the sandbox reports a failure (`error`, W118) but not its recovery, so a host that lists failures, like the playground's test page, keeps one after the component draws again. Design a *recovered* event with the others, so a host can clear what it listed.

tasks.name: Split long source files into modules
tasks.description:
Some CompMD source files are too long to read well, even after their tests moved out. `processor/src/processor.rs` is one example.

## Scan
Cover every crate and package in `compmd`: processor, render, sandbox, registry, wasm, editor and website. Look at code, not only tests. List the long source files and judge each one for readability. About 400 lines is a guideline, not a threshold (see `docs/code/rust.md#tests` and `CLAUDE.md`, Testing).

## Split
- Split the long files into modules along their responsibilities, with no change in behaviour.
- Keep public APIs the same, unless a change makes them simpler.
- Leave files that read fine as one unit as they are, and note which ones and why.

## Done when
`cargo make ci` and `pnpm -r lint` are green, and Rust coverage is at least 99%.

## Result (2026-11-06)

Lines are before → after, the file's own lines; every public path stays as it was (`compmd::tree::…` is re-exported, `@compmd/processor`'s `OpenDocument` too).

### Split

| `processor/src/tree.rs` | 955 → 550 | `tree/components.rs` (CompMD's nodes: interpolations, components, params), `tree/definitions.rs` (definitions, signatures, declared types) |

tasks.name: Website: no unstyled flash between guide pages on the dev server
tasks.description:
Following a link in a guide's contents shows the page unstyled for a moment before its styles apply.

## Cause (to confirm)
The built site inlines its CSS in each page's `<head>` (`dist/guides/…/index.html` has `<style>` blocks), so it shouldn't flash. On the dev server the CSS reaches the page only through `src/spec.ts`'s imports of `base.css` and `spec.css`, which Vite applies after the script runs: every full page load paints first without styles.

- Confirm in the dev server and the built site (`pnpm preview`), in Chrome and WebKit.
- Make the dev server's guide and spec pages carry their stylesheets in `<head>`, as the build does, without loading them twice in the build.

## Tests
A browser test that the first paint of a guide page is styled (e.g. its body background is the site's, before any script runs).

tasks.name: Sandbox: tell the host when a view's layout has settled
tasks.description:
A view's page keeps changing size after `render()` returns: each frame takes its height only once it has drawn and reported it, and a frame's own frames later still. Nothing tells the host when that is over. Tests, printing and scrolling to a link's target all need to know, and today guess.

## The problem, as found (2026-11-02)
Three browser tests failed now and then, all in a full `cargo make ci`, where many browser tests run at once:
- `vite/test/example.test.ts`, the inspector's Data test, WebKit (2 of 7 runs).
- `guides/test/part-3.test.ts`, the spoiler test, WebKit.
- `guides/test/part-2.test.ts`, the styled page's link test, Chrome.

Each clicked something that a frame above it then moved: the inspector's tab sat at y=293 when clicked and at y=396 three seconds later, so the click landed on the old spot and the tab stayed on Console.

**Why Playwright can't prevent it:** before a click it scrolls the element into view, waits until its box is the same in two animation frames, and hit-tests the point; but the click is a real mouse event at coordinates, sent after that check. A frame reporting its height in between moves the target. No test can close that gap by reading the position again.

## Today's workarounds (replace them with this)
- `vite/example/index.html`: `#page` has a fixed height (`24rem`), so the inspector under it doesn't move; `vite/test/example.test.ts` checks after the click that the tab is selected.
- `guides/test/part-3.test.ts`: `stillAt(locator)` polls until the spoiler's top is the same for 100 ms, after waiting for the `reviews` frame's text.
- `guides/test/part-2.test.ts`: the link test waits for the app's stylesheet to apply before clicking.

## To reproduce
1. Undo a workaround (for example the fixed height in `vite/example/index.html`).
2. Load the machine: `pnpm --dir guides test` in the background.
3. Meanwhile, `pnpm --dir vite exec vitest run test/example.test.ts` a few times.
4. To see the movement, log the element's `boundingBox().y` right after the click and again 3 s later (`page.waitForTimeout(3000)`): in host mode in WebKit it moves by about 100 px.

## The change
- **`@compmd/sandbox`:** a view says when its layout has settled: every use mounted, every frame (at any depth) drawn and its height reported and applied, with no render in progress. Proposed: `view.settled(): Promise<void>`, which resolves once that holds after the latest `render()` (a later `render()` starts a new one), and possibly a `settled` event (`view.on("settled", …)`). In both page modes, host and frame. A frame that never reports (it hung, W118) must not keep it pending forever: settle with it stopped, as the observer records it.
- **The protocol** (`docs/sandbox-protocol.md`): what a frame sends once it has drawn and sized itself, if the existing size messages don't already say it; a frame with frames of its own reports once they have.
- **Docs:** `sandbox/README.md` (the API, with an example), `docs/running-components-in-the-sandbox.md`.
- **Use it:** the three tests above wait for `settled()` (through the page, e.g. a `data-settled` attribute or a function the example exposes) instead of their workarounds; remove `stillAt`; decide whether the Vite example keeps its fixed height for its own sake.

## Who else needs it
- Printing a guide to PDF (CMD-157) must wait until every frame has its height, or the PDF has cut or overlapping frames.
- A page that scrolls to a link's target (`#section`) after load lands in the wrong place while frames above it still grow.

## Tests
`@compmd/sandbox` browser tests, Chrome and WebKit, host and frame mode: `settled()` resolves only after a frame whose height arrives late (a component that draws after a delay) has been sized; a second `render()` re-arms it; a hung frame doesn't keep it pending.

notes.text: Seen again 2026-11-02 in a full CI run: `guides/test/part-2.test.ts`, the styled page’s link test in Chrome; the link was clicked after the stylesheet applied, and the dialog stayed empty. The stylesheet wait isn’t enough.

Review the design in review (CompMD `4c7222e`: spec §7.4 `busy`, the sandbox README *When the page has settled*, the protocol’s *Settled*, render’s `page.drawn()`); once approved, implement it. → Approved in review (CompMD `4c7222e`): `busy` in spec §7.4, `page.drawn()`, `view.settled()`, `settled`, `data-compmd-settled`, the protocol’s *Settled*.

CompMD `e8ebfcd` (design `4c7222e`): `busy` in the contract and bindings, `page.drawn()`, render’s `drawn`; frames settle bottom-up and report `settled {seen}`; `view.settled()`, `settled`, `data-compmd-settled`; `draw` calls `busy`; the three test workarounds replaced. Stylesheets are waited for too. CI green.
Approved in review: CompMD `e8ebfcd`, `busy`, `page.drawn()` and the view’s `settled`, with the three test workarounds replaced.

tasks.name: Sandbox: a document's own images in frame mode
tasks.description:
In frame mode the whole page renders in one strict frame, whose policy is `img-src data: blob:` (`sandbox/src/build/policy.ts`, `strictPolicy`). So a document's own Markdown images, `![](https://…/photo.png)` and `![](./logo.png)`, don't load in frame mode, while they do in host mode. The rule exists so a strict component's code can't make requests (no network); it also catches images the document's author wrote, which aren't component code.

## To settle first (with the user, before code)
- Whether frame mode should show a document's own images at all, and from where: relative paths (the document's files, which the host has), and remote URLs (which tell their origin that the page was viewed, as §15 *Privacy* says of images).
- How, without giving component code the network: for example, the host's page fetching the document's images and passing them in as `blob:` URLs (the policy allows `blob:` already), or the page frame's renderer asking the host for each image. Not by widening `img-src` for the strict frame, which component code in it would get too.
- What a missing or refused image shows (its alt text).

## Then
The change in `@compmd/sandbox` (and `@compmd/render` if the renderer asks for images), docs in `sandbox/README.md` and `docs/running-components-in-the-sandbox.md`, and browser tests: the same document's local and remote images in both modes; component code in the strict frame still can't load an image from the network.

notes.text: Decided with the user: **1A** frame mode shows the document’s own images. **2A** the host page fetches each image in the tree it sent (no credentials, no `Referer`) and posts it as a Blob; the frame shows a `blob:` URL, its CSP unchanged. **3A** remote images load without asking, as host mode does today. **Q4** alt text while missing, failed or loading. No spec change now; asking before images is CMD-183 (backlog).

CompMD `dd9dcac`. Frame mode: the page frame asks its parent for each image (`image`/`fetched` in the protocol); the host page fetches only images of trees it sent, no credentials, no `Referer`, image types only; shown as `blob:`, CSP unchanged. Render `images` option: alt text until loaded or when refused. Limit: remote images without CORS show alt text. Browser tests in Chrome and WebKit. CI green.
Approved by the user after the sprint review.

tasks.name: Sandbox: frame mode's theme tokens before the first mount

tasks.name: `loadData`, the playground asking before data from a new origin, and the guides
tasks.description:
Agreed with the user (2026-11-03): one step a host calls for its remote data, which asks the reader about new origins by itself (spec §8.6), so a host complies by default; `allowOrigins` stays for hosts that fetch on their own. Then an example in the playground, and a section in each guide.

## `loadData` (`@compmd/sandbox`, host side)
- `loadData(urls, { configured, document, ask?, answers?, fetch? })`: the remote URLs a render needs (the processor's `sources(request).remote`) → `{ allowedOrigins, remote }` for the request: `allowOrigins` for the origins, then each URL of an allowed origin fetched with `credentials: "omit"` (`{ text, contentType }`); a failed fetch is left out (the processor reports F026 and loads the fallback).
- It takes URLs, not a request, so it needs no processor in the page, and works with a worker's list.
- Not interactive (no reader): `ask` answers deny, and nothing is fetched from unconfigured origins.
- Tests in Chrome and WebKit: fetched from allowed origins only, without credentials; a denied origin is F028 with the fallback; a failed fetch F026 with the fallback.

## The playground (`@compmd/devtools`, `editor/`)
- Allowing an origin is decided when the document is validated, so it means opening the document again (as for packs that arrive). The worker reports the remote URLs a document needs once typing pauses; the page calls `loadData` (the question is the page's, never the worker's or a frame's) and reopens the document with `allowedOrigins` and `remote`.
- An example document: data from npm's registry (`https://registry.npmjs.org/@comp-markdown/mermaid/latest`, which answers cross-origin requests), with a `fallback` file, showing the pack's latest version and description; the playground asks the first time, and the About says what npm learns.
- Tests: the devtools' processing asks once per origin and reopens with the data; the example renders its fallback before an answer.

## The guides
- **Author's Guide**, chapter 6 (data from files and the web): when a page asks the reader before loading data from a site, what the reader sees meanwhile (the fallback), and why to write a `fallback`.
- **Developer's Guide**, chapter 6 (data and inputs): `loadData` in the host's loop, configured origins, the answers store (`localAnswers`, `list`, `forget`), asking in the host's own UI, `allowOrigins` for hosts that fetch themselves, and that §8.6's MUST is the host's.
- Each with a **Try it** link to the playground's example; the guides' tests cover the new text's documents.

notes.text: Builds on CMD-170’s `allowOrigins` (CompMD `64600c6`, in review): the dependency was dropped so this can start before the end-of-sprint review; review the two together.
Correction to the description: a failed fetch *with* a `fallback` uses it with no diagnostic (§8.6); F026 is only without one. `loadData` and its tests follow the spec.

CompMD `ab1e553` (from `git log`). `loadData` (asks, fetches without credentials or Referer); processor `sources` gains `disallowed`; devtools: worker reports URLs, page asks and reopens; playground `?doc=remote` (npm registry, fallback); Author’s and Developer’s Guide ch. 6, ch. 19, 21. Tests: Rust, wasm, sandbox browser, devtools, playground end to end in Chrome. CI green, lint included.

tasks.name: Render: map between the page's elements and the source they came from
tasks.description:
An app that embeds `@compmd/render` can't ask which source range made an element, or which elements a source range drew. The renderer has this (origins, spec §12.3, with each block's shift after splices in `blocks.ts`), but keeps it private. An app holding the tree can't redo it: after `page.splice`, the origins of kept blocks are behind the text.

## Decided with the user (2026-11-03)
1. **Two calls, on `Page` and `Region`:** `sourceOf(node)` gives the range that made a DOM node (text nodes too), or its nearest mapped parent's; `elementsAt(offset)` gives the elements of the innermost node whose range holds the offset. No range form yet.
2. **`Source`** has the shape of `Origin` (`start`/`end` with `line`, `column`, `offset`), in the current text. Offsets in code points; `codePointOffset` and `utf16Offset` exported for editors.
3. **What maps to what:** interpolated text and `value` → the node holding it; a `compmd` definition's body → the invocation; a component's own DOM → the component; the footnotes list → each definition; what the renderer adds (↩) → its nearest mapped parent. Without `origins: true`, nothing.
4. **Storage:** a `WeakMap` in the renderer, no `data-*` attributes.
5. **`@compmd/sandbox`, both modes, same calls on the view:** `reveal(offset)` scrolls to what it drew and marks it briefly; `rectsAt(offset)` gives its boxes in the host's coordinates; opt-in `onPointed({ source })` reports the source of what the reader clicked. Frame mode as protocol messages, in `protocol.schema.json`.
6. **The playground:** a click in the preview moves the editor's caret; moving the caret scrolls the preview.

## Docs
Documented well: TSDoc on every call (what, arguments, what it gives back, an example), the render and sandbox READMEs' API sections, the sandbox protocol doc, and the Developer's Guide.

## Tests
Both calls through renders and splices (kept blocks shifted), each mapping rule, both sandbox modes, the playground.

notes.text: CompMD `ea05b85`. `sourceOf`/`elementsAt` on Page and Region, `reveal`; frame protocol v3 (`reveal`, `rects`, `point`, `pointed`; host end checks shapes); sandbox `view.reveal`, `rectsAt`, `pointed` (opt-in by listening); playground click to caret, caret to preview. Messages are in render’s frame protocol, not the sandbox schema. Not seen in a real browser playground yet. CI green.
Approved in review with no comments. CompMD `ea05b85`.

tasks.name: Faster CI and e2e tests, and Linux problems caught locally with Docker before pushing
tasks.description:
`cargo make ci` takes many minutes, the browser (e2e) tests are the slowest part, and some failures show only on GitHub's Linux runners: at 0.4.0 the Pages workflow failed with `/ (phone, light) is 1px wider than the window` (`website/scripts/check.ts`), which passed locally on macOS, most likely because of the runner's fonts.

## Scope
- **Measure first:** where `cargo make ci` and the GitHub workflows (`ci.yml`, the Pages workflow, `release.yml`) spend their time, per step and per test file.
- **Speed up CI:** parallel jobs or steps, caching (cargo, pnpm, Playwright browsers, wasm builds), nothing built twice; without weakening any test or budget.
- **Speed up the e2e tests:** the Playwright tests in `sandbox`, `registry`, `vite`, `create-pack`, `editor`, `guides` and `website`: shared servers and browsers, fewer fixed waits, parallel files where they don't share ports.
- **Docker, locally:** one command that runs CI (or the failing part, such as `pnpm --dir website check`) in a container like the runner, Ubuntu with its fonts, so Linux-only failures show before a push.

## Done when
The timings before and after are recorded, CI is faster with every check kept, and the Docker command reproduces the runner's result for the website check.

tasks.name: The release workflow's crates job reads each crate's version without a Cargo.lock
tasks.description:
The `crates` job of `.github/workflows/release.yml` failed at `v0.4.0` (run [41727981179](https://github.com/comp-markdown/compmd/actions/runs/41727981179), job `crates`, step *Publish*), the first release whose crates it was to publish (0.3.0's `compmd` was published by hand). Nothing was published by it; `compmd` 0.4.0 was then published by hand from the tag (`RELEASING.md`, *By hand*). ## What happened ```mermaid flowchart TD A["publish compmd-markdown markdown-rs/Cargo.toml"] --> B["cargo pkgid --manifest-path markdown-rs/Cargo.toml"] B -->|"markdown-rs is a workspace of its own,
with no Cargo.lock in the checkout"| C["error: a Cargo.lock must exist for this command"] C -->|"the pipeline's status is sed's, 0,
so bash -e goes on"| D["version is empty"] D --> E["curl crates.io/api/v1/crates/compmd-markdown/ fails"] E --> F["cargo publish compmd-markdown"] F --> G["error: crate compmd-markdown@0.1.0 already exists"] G -->|"exit 101, bash -e stops"| H["compmd is never tried"] ``` The log: ```text error: a Cargo.lock must exist for this command Updating crates.io index error: crate compmd-markdown@0.1.0 already exists on crates.io index ``` The step, as it is: ```sh publish() { version="$(cargo pkgid --manifest-path "$2" -p "$1" | sed 's/.*@//')" if curl -sf -A "comp-markdown/compmd release workflow" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$1/$version" > /dev/null; then echo "$1@$version is on crates.io already" else cargo publish --manifest-path "$2" -p "$1" fi } publish compmd-markdown markdown-rs/Cargo.toml publish compmd Cargo.toml ``` `compmd`'s own version would have read fine: the repository root has a `Cargo.lock`. The *release* job's own tag check (`cargo pkgid -p compmd`) runs at the root too, so it is not affected. ## The fix - Read the version without a lock file: `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --manifest-path "$2"`, the package named `$1` (with `jq`, on the runner, or `node -p`, as the *Stage* step does). - Fail loudly on an empty version (`set -o pipefail`, or a check that `version` isn't empty) instead of going on, so a wrong read never reaches `cargo publish`. - Keep the order and the skip: `compmd-markdown` first, only when crates.io lacks its version, then `compmd`. - Comments in the workflow, and `RELEASING.md` section 3, say what it does, as now; record there that `0.4.0`'s crate was published by hand, as `0.3.0`'s was. ## Checking it, before the next release The job runs only on a tag and publishes for real, so check the step's script on its own first: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["the step's script, locally,
a fresh clone with submodules"] --> B["both versions read:
compmd-markdown 0.1.0, compmd 0.4.0"] B --> C["with cargo publish replaced by echo:
both skipped, as on crates.io already"] C --> D["the next tag v0.4.1 / v0.5.0:
compmd-markdown skipped, compmd published"] ``` - In a clean clone (`git clone --recurse-submodules`), so `markdown-rs/` has no `Cargo.lock`, as in CI. - Ideally in the Docker image of CMD-191, like the runner. - On the next release, the `crates` job is green after the author approves the `crates-io` environment, and `cargo search compmd` gives the new version.

tasks.name: Shiki and Temml shipped once, host mode loading them from the frames’ files
tasks.description:
Shiki (code highlighting, about 465 KB gzipped with its 63 grammars) and Temml (math, 204 KB) are each built **twice** into every app made with `@compmd/vite`, and the website's deploy holds four copies of each (the site and the playground, two apps). Decided with the user (2026-11-04): **host mode loads both from the frames' own files, as frames share React from `compmd/libs/`**; one copy per app, which a page and its frames cache once. ## Why there are two copies Not two sources: one npm source, bundled by **two builds** that run in different windows. ```mermaid flowchart TB npm["@shikijs/* and temml
(npm, one source)"] npm --> fb["the frames' build
sandbox/scripts/frames.ts, ahead of time"] npm --> ab["the app's own Vite build
it bundles what @compmd/sandbox imports"] fb --> fc["compmd/chunks/cpp-D4FY7gDX.js, temml-….js
copied into each app by @compmd/vite"] ab --> ac["assets/cpp-BtFpP2dM.js, temml-….js"] fc --> frames["loaded by the frames
(frame mode's page frame, host mode's use frames)"] ac --> page["loaded by the app's page
(host mode only: hostPage's shikiHighlight() and temmlMath())"] ``` - `sandbox/src/sandbox.ts`, `hostPage`: `createPage(container, { math: temmlMath(), highlight: shikiHighlight(), … })`. Their dynamic imports (`import("@shikijs/core")`, the grammars in `highlight/languages.ts`, `import("temml")`) are what Vite bundles into the app's `assets/`. - Both copies load lazily, the first time a page has a code block or math. **Frame mode** fetches only the frames' copy; the `assets/` one is dead weight in the deploy. **Host mode** fetches the `assets/` copy for the page and the frames' copy for code or math in a framed use: a reader downloads both. - Found in the build (2026-11-04): `website/dist/assets/cpp-BtFpP2dM.js`, `website/dist/compmd/chunks/cpp-D4FY7gDX.js`, and the same two under `website/dist/playground/`; `editor/dist/` has its two; `sandbox/dist/frames/chunks/cpp-D4FY7gDX.js` is the frames' source of `compmd/`. **Why not the other way round:** the frames are sandboxed with an opaque origin, and their policy loads scripts from `compmd/` only, so they can't use the app's `assets/`. The app's page can load `compmd/`, which is the app's own deploy, served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` already. **Rejected:** host mode as a wrapper around one trusted frame. It would remove the copy, but trusted components would lose the app's state, context and direct `host` (spec §15: trusted is the host's own code, outside a sandbox), the page would need a height and its own styles, and editors that render block by block wouldn't fit. Frame mode already is that one path, for an app that needs nothing inline. ## The change ```mermaid flowchart TB npm["@shikijs/* and temml (npm)"] --> fb["the frames' build"] fb --> entries["compmd/highlight.js, compmd/math.js (new, fixed names)
runtime.js
compmd/chunks/: the grammars, Shiki's core, Temml, shared by all three"] entries --> frames["the frames: runtime.js, as now"] entries --> page["the app's page, host mode:
import(new URL('highlight.js', base)) the first time it has a code block,
import(new URL('math.js', base)) the first time it has math"] ab["the app's own Vite build"] -.->|"no Shiki, no Temml:
host mode no longer imports them"| none["assets/"] ``` 1. **The frames' build** (`sandbox/scripts/frames.ts`): two more entries beside `runtime.js`, with fixed names, `highlight.js` (exporting `shikiHighlight`) and `math.js` (exporting Temml's typesetter), built in the same build, so they share their chunks with `runtime.js`: still one copy of each grammar. 2. **`hostPage`** (`sandbox/src/sandbox.ts`): a `CodeHighlighter` and a `MathRenderer` that, on first use, `import(/* @vite-ignore */ new URL("highlight.js", base))` (and `math.js`), from the frames' folder the app gives `createSandbox` as `base` (`frameUrl`), then delegate to what they export; `typesetMath(load)` and `highlightWith` already take a loader. Until it loads, code and math show as they do now, as text. 3. **Exports stay:** `shikiHighlight()` and `temmlMath()` remain for a host that renders with `createPage` itself; that host bundles them, as now. 4. **A host whose page has a content security policy** allows scripts from where `compmd/` is served (its own origin, or the frames' origin when `base` is another): the README says so. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant P as the app's page (host mode) participant C as compmd/ (the frames' files) participant F as a use's frame Note over P: the first code block on the page P->>C: import highlight.js C-->>P: highlight.js + Shiki's core, engine, themes, the block's grammar Note over F: a code block in a framed use's slot F->>C: runtime.js imports the same chunks C-->>F: from the browser's cache: the same files ``` ## Done when - **One copy per app:** a test of `@compmd/vite`'s example build (`vite/test/example.test.ts`) checks that `assets/` has no Shiki or Temml chunk (no `cpp-*.js`, `temml-*.js`, `@shikijs/core`'s code) and that `compmd/` has `highlight.js` and `math.js`; the website's build (`website/scripts/check.ts`) the same. - **Highlighting and math still work in host mode**, light and dark: the sandbox's browser tests (`sandbox/test/view.test.ts`, *code blocks* and *math*, host mode) pass, now loading from `compmd/`; and in frame mode, unchanged. - **Docs:** the sandbox README's *Code blocks* (where Shiki comes from in each mode, what it costs: once per app), the table of *Where the page renders*, and `docs/running-components-in-the-sandbox.md` decision 4; guides chapter 11, *What the frames load* (`highlight.js`, `math.js`). ## Not in this task - The website deploying two apps, the site and the playground, each with its own `compmd/`: their files are the same (the same hashes), so one shared `compmd/` would halve the website's deploy. Deploy size only, since a reader downloads one app's copy; a task of its own if wanted.

# Review compmd.hakanserce.com as an awareness site

Review `compmd.hakanserce.com` as a professional website that promotes and creates awareness of CompMD.

## Star component (using `draw` from `@compmd/pack/component`)

A host-language component written with `draw` that draws five stars from a single `value` parameter using inline SVG — no d3, no manual mount. Color changes as the count goes higher: 1–2 muted gray, 3 amber, 4 green, 5 deep green.

`draw` handles mounting, updates, scheme changes, error fallbacks, and `busy` tracking automatically.

```js component=star
import { draw } from "@compmd/pack/component";

export interface Params {
  value: number;
}

const colors = ["#97a3b1", "#97a3b1", "#d4a017", "#2e7d32", "#1a7e1a"];
const emptyLight = "#5b6776";
const emptyDark = "#97a3b1";
const starPath = "M9 0 L9.88 3.09 L13.09 3.09 L10.38 5.88 L11.25 9 L8.75 7.12 L6.38 5.88 L3.67 3.09 L6.88 3.09 L7.75 0 Z";
const size = 18;
const gap = 6;

export default draw<Params>(
  ({ value }, { scheme }) => {
    const n = Math.min(Math.max(Math.round(Number(value ?? 0)), 0), 5);
    const empty = scheme === "dark" ? emptyDark : emptyLight;
    const accent = colors[Math.min(Math.max(n - 1, 0), 4)];

    const stars = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      const fill = i < n ? accent : "none";
      stars.push(
        `<path d="${starPath}" transform="translate(${i * (size + gap) + size / 2},12)" fill="${fill}" stroke="${empty}" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/>`
      );
    }

    return `<svg viewBox="0 0 130 24" width="130" height="24" style="display:inline-block;vertical-align:middle">${stars.join("")}</svg>`;
  },
  { role: "img" }
);
```

Signature in the document:

```compmd component=star signature
params:
  value: number
```

Usage:

```
:star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=4}
```

## Current state

The site is well-built, technically solid, and professional. It loads fast (45 KB gzipped, ~0.77 s paint on a mid-range phone over fast 3G), looks clean in light and dark mode, and states what CompMD is in the hero. The live interactive demo is a genuine strength — visitors can edit CompMD and see it render immediately, no sign-up required.

::: box {padding=m background=subtle border-radius=m}
**:value[2]{of=(string(size(md.data.strengths.filter(s, s.category == "messaging"))))} messaging strengths**

### Strengths

| Area | What works |
|---|---|
| Value proposition | Hero line "Markdown with components. Readable as text, rendered as a page." is clear and differentiated. |
| Live demo | Editable document beside its rendered page; visitors experience the product immediately. |
| Key differentiator | "Still Markdown" section — CompMD degrades gracefully in plain renderers — gets real space. |
| Performance | Meets its own budgets: 100 KB gzipped cap (at 45 KB), paint under 1 s on phone. |
| Design | Consistent light/dark palette (ink `#1b2430`, accent `#3557c4`), serif headings, sans body, system fonts. |
| Search | Site-wide MiniSearch on every page, built at prerender time. |
| Security | Dedicated "Safe to open" section explains the sandbox model. |
| Analytics | GoatCounter without cookies; no consent banner needed. |

### Improvement priority flow

```mermaid {theme=default}
graph TD
    A[Add OG tags + favicon] --> B[Replace hero example]
    B --> C[Clarify stability + install line]
    C --> D[Add social proof / real examples]

    style B fill:#e9edf1,stroke:#3557c4,stroke-width:2px

```

### Improvements by category

| Category | Item | Rating | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content / messaging | Replace hero example ("Launch week" about building CompMD) with an audience-relevant document (README, release notes, trip checklist) | :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=4} | First impression; visitors see what they can build |
| Content / messaging | Add "who is this for / why choose CompMD" line | :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=3} | Helps visitors self-identify |
| Content / messaging | Add social proof / real-world examples, changelog or roadmap link | :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=3} | Converts interest into trust |
| Content / messaging | Clarify stability: "0.x while draft" is vague; one accurate install line + 1.0 expectation | :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=3} | Reduces uncertainty for adopters |
| Look | Add visual interest to monochrome design; subtle section variation, architecture diagram for "Under the hood" | :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=3} | More engaging awareness site |

| Technical / SEO | Verify dark-mode contrast; add "skip to content" link | :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=2} | Accessibility |

## Recommended order

1. **Open Graph / Twitter Card tags + favicon** — low effort, high impact on sharing and discovery. Rating: :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=5}
2. **Hero example swap + "who is this for"** — low effort, high impact on first impression. Rating: :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=4}

6. **Unify header/footer across pages** — medium effort, brand consistency. Rating: :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=3}
7. **Sitemap, robots.txt, JSON-LD, contrast check, skip link** — low effort, polish. Rating: :star[☆☆☆☆☆]{value=2}

Several points need user decisions first: the hero example choice, the accurate install line, whether to add email capture. These mirror how the site's own design doc settles aesthetics interactively.

## Claude's own scan (2026-11-06)

A second look, at the source (`website/`, `editor/`) and the live site, before going through the list together. Where it differs from the findings above, it says so.

### Already done, or smaller than the list says

- **Favicon:** every page already has one (`logo/icon.svg`). Missing only a PNG `apple-touch-icon` for platforms that don't take SVG.
- **Header and footer:** the landing page, the spec and the guides already share `Header.svelte` and `Footer.svelte`. Only the playground has its own header, as an app; it lacks a **Guides** link (it has Spec and GitHub) and search. So the "unify" item shrinks to adding Guides to the playground's header.
- **Install line:** the landing page has one (`npm install @compmd/vite @compmd/processor @compmd/sandbox`), which is right. But the note under it is **wrong**: it says `@compmd/sandbox` and `@compmd/vite` are "to follow", and both have been on npm since 0.2.0 (now 0.5.0). A plain bug, no decision needed.
- **Stability:** the README already has a *Status: draft* line, and the spec page a *Draft* banner. The landing page has only the small `0.x while the spec is a draft` note, and the playground's About says nothing. One sentence near the install line and one in the About, in the README's words, is enough; no banner.
- **Spec page "plain GFM HTML":** not so. It has its contents beside the text, a scroll-spy, Shiki highlighting and the draft banner (design decision 6). Callouts are a nice-to-have, low.

### New findings

- **Numbers on the page have drifted.** "188 cases" (in *Under the hood* and *Where next*): the conformance set has 209 now. "808 KB gzipped" and "0.30 ms" are hard-coded too. These should be computed by the site's build (count the cases, measure the built `.wasm`), or the page should stop giving exact numbers.
- **Every guides page has the Developer's Guide's description**, the shelf, the Author's Guide and every chapter (`website/guides/index.html` is the only `<meta name="description">`). Each page needs its own, such as the chapter's first paragraph. That matters for search results and link previews as much as Open Graph does.
- **The playground has no description** at all (`editor/index.html`).
- **No 404 page of the site's own:** a wrong address gets GitHub's default. A `404.html` with the site's header and search is cheap.
- **No `robots.txt` or `sitemap.xml`** (confirmed: both 404 live). The sitemap can come from the pages the search index already lists.
- **GitHub on a phone:** under 30rem the header hides GitHub, on the reasoning that it is a card in *Where next*. But only the landing page has *Where next*: on a phone, the spec and the guides have no link to the repository at all. My suggestion: GitHub (and npm) in the footer, the header as it is.
- **The design doc has drifted from the site:** decision 7's install line is `@compmd/processor @compmd/render`, and its hero sketch is a `report.comp.md` with stats. To update with whatever we settle here.
- **Figures the design doc planned and never built:** a small figure per *Why* beat and a sandbox figure in *Safe to open*. That's the real gap behind "add visual interest", rather than the palette being monochrome.

### Where I see it differently

- **Open Graph:** agreed it comes first. But make the 1200×630 image at build time, from the logo and the hero line (the build already has Playwright to render it), so it can't go stale, rather than a hand-made image.
- **JSON-LD:** leave it out. A spec site gets no rich result from it (YAGNI).
- **Email capture:** I'd say no for now. It needs an outside service holding readers' addresses, against the site's "nothing that identifies a reader" (design decision 8) and the tone of *Safe to open*. Instead: a "Watch releases on GitHub" link and a link to the changelog. GitHub's releases already have an Atom feed.
- **Social proof:** leave it out until there is some. Made-up proof costs more trust than none. Link the changelog and, if there is one, a roadmap.
- **Hero example:** agreed, replace *Launch week*. My suggestion is **release notes**: spec §16's own example (`conformance/examples/spec-16-release-notes`), a document the audience writes, and one that shows a grid, a value from data and an input. Not a trip checklist: `trip.md` already shows plain Markdown further down.
- **"Who is this for":** agreed, one line under the lede, for writers who want pages from Markdown and developers who put documents in their app.
- **"Where next" cards:** fine as they are. The list above misses that a Guides card is already there.

### To decide together

1. The hero example: release notes, or another?
2. Email capture: no (my view), or yes and with which service?
3. The numbers: computed at build time, or no exact numbers?
4. The early-stage sentence: wording, and whether it goes on the landing page and the About, the README's already being there.
5. The Open Graph image: generated at build time from the logo and hero line?
6. GitHub on phones: in the footer?
7. The playground's header: add Guides, and search?

# W118 component error is sticky: after a component throws, fixing the source does not recover In the CompMD playground, manually editing a document that causes a component to throw (W118) leaves the component stuck in error state even after the source is fixed. ## Reproduction 1. Open the playground with a document whose frontmatter has a plots list: ```md --- md: version: 1 plots: - {number: 1, gardener: Maya Okafor} - {number: 2, gardener: Tomás Reyes} - {number: 3, gardener: ""} - {number: 4, gardener: Priya Nair} - {number: 5, gardener: ""} --- :: plot-map[Plots 1, 2 and 4 are taken; plots 3 and 5 are free] {plots=(md.doc.plots)} ```svelte component=plot-map runtime=svelte@5
{#each plots as plot} {plot.number} {/each}
``` ```compmd component=plot-map signature params: plots: array ``` ``` 2. Edit the plots list so the first item is just `-` with no content yet (empty list entry while typing). 3. `plot.gardener` reads null on a null/empty list item → component throws → W118: `plot-map: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'gardener')`. 4. Fix the content (fill in valid values for all list items). 5. Expected: the component re-renders with the fixed data. 6. Actual: the component stays in W118 error state and never recovers. The error state is sticky — once a component throws, fixing the source does not trigger a re-render or recovery. ## Files likely involved - `render/src/render.ts` — component mount/update/error handling - `render/src/component.ts` — mount contract and failure handling - `pack/src/component.ts` — `draw` error wrapping (`context.fail` on throw) - `editor/**` — playground live-edit loop ## Expected behavior After a component recovers (its source no longer throws), the renderer should re-mount it and clear the W118 error, showing the rendered output again.

notes.text: Fixed in compmd e29c2bf. Cause: after a failure the renderer empties the box before the next update (spec 7.4), but the Svelte binding kept updating its old instance, whose DOM was gone. Both bindings now remount at that update. Also found: React 19 reports a render error instead of throwing it, so React showed an empty box and no W118; the binding now throws it. Tests in render/test/bindings.test.ts. cargo make ci green.

Reported by another project (2026-11-06) against `@compmd/vite` 0.5.0.

## The bug
`integrities()` in [`vite/src/packs.ts`](vite/src/packs.ts#L162-L187) keeps only the first YAML document of `pnpm-lock.yaml` that has `packages`. Its comment expects that first document to be pnpm's settings, without packages. Since pnpm 10/11, a project that pins its toolchain with `devEngines` (`packageManager` and/or `runtime`, `onFail: "download"`) gets two documents: an environment lockfile, with its own `importers` and `packages` for the pinned pnpm and Node, then the project's lockfile. The first wins, so no pack is found and every pack's integrity is `null` in the generated runtime (`packs:{"@comp-markdown/mermaid":[{version:"0.1.1",integrity:null,…}]}`).

## Fix
- Merge `packages` from every document, with the same key normalisation (strip a leading `/` and a peer suffix `(…)`). The environment document only holds pnpm and Node, so merging is harmless.
- **Warn at build time** when the app has a lock file but an installed pack has no integrity in it (decided with the user), instead of writing `null` silently. Update [`docs/vite.md` V1](docs/vite.md#:~:text=V1.%20Where%20a%20release) with the rule, and fix the code comment.
- A `CHANGELOG.md` line.

## Check while fixing
The report says documents that pin a pack by integrity then pass unchecked. V1 says a release without integrity makes a document's `integrity` key fail to match, which the processor reports. Confirm which is true with a test, and fix whatever doesn't follow V1.

## Tests
- A fixture `pnpm-lock.yaml` with an environment document before the project document gives the pack's integrity.
- The single-document and `package-lock.json` cases are unchanged.
- A pack missing from an existing lock file gives the new warning; no lock file gives none.
- A document pinning an integrity, built without one for its pack, gets the processor's mismatch.

## Done when
`cargo make ci` and `pnpm -r lint` are green.

tasks.name: The frames load from a custom scheme in WebKit
tasks.description:
Found by another Tauri host of CompMD (2026-11-09): on macOS and Linux WebKit, a frame document served from a custom scheme (`compmd://`, an app's own scheme) can't load its runtime. A sandboxed frame's origin is opaque, and WebKit's `'self'` falls back to the response URL's origin only for `http` and `https`. On any other scheme `'self'` matches nothing, so `script-src 'self'` refuses the frame's own `runtime.js`. `style-src 'self'` and `font-src 'self'` fail the same way. Over `http` (`atm serve`, Windows' `http://<scheme>.localhost`) it works.

## Change (decided with the user)
- `buildFrames` takes the frames' own source from the host: an optional `source`, such as `app://localhost/frames/`, a source with a path, not a bare scheme, so a strict frame can't load scripts from elsewhere on that scheme (a host that later serves packs' code there).
- `strictPolicy`, `permissivePolicy` and the permissive frame's second, narrowed policy (`frame/narrow.ts`) add that source next to every `'self'`: `script-src`, `style-src`, `font-src`.
- Without `source`, the policies stay as they are (`'self'` alone, for hosts that serve over http).
- Check the source's form: a CSP source expression with a path; refuse a value that would widen the policy (`*`, a bare scheme followed by nothing, `;`), as `narrowed` does for pack origins.
- The sandbox README's *Serving the frame documents* says when a host needs it: any scheme but http and https.

## Tests
- `build/policy.test.ts` and `build/build.test.ts`: the source in each directive, and nothing added without it; a bad source refused.
- `frame/narrow.test.ts`: the narrowed policy keeps it.
- If the browser tests can serve from a custom scheme in WebKit, a test that a strict frame loads there; otherwise say so in the outcome, and an application's own check covers it.

tasks.description:
Decided with the user 2026-11-09: CompMD gets a Tauri plugin that serves the sandbox's frames from a scheme of the app's own, and an example app that tests it in a real webview (WebKitGTK in CI). It gates the 0.6.0 release (CMD-214). Another Tauri host of CompMD planned the same plugin and to move it into CompMD; an application waits for it.

A design doc in `docs/` (decisions first, plain wording, no mention of any host), reviewed with the user before code: the scheme's handler is security code.

## To settle in it
- **The crate:** name (`tauri-plugin-compmd`), place in the repo (outside the main Cargo workspace or in it), how it is released (with the implementation's version, by the release workflow, like `compmd`).
- **What it serves:** the frames `buildFrames` wrote, from a folder the app bundles as a resource, at content-hashed paths (`/frames/<hash>/`, a `frames.json` naming the hash) so a WebKit cache never serves an old frame after an upgrade; the scheme's name the app's choice.
- **The handler's rules:** GET only (405 with why), paths only under the build's folder, no `.` or `..` part (404 with why); `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, the type by extension, `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- **The frames' `base` and `source`:** a command or a Rust call that gives `base`; the `source` the app passes to `buildFrames` (CMD-211), per platform (`<scheme>://localhost/frames/` on macOS and Linux, `http://<scheme>.localhost/frames/` on Windows and Android).
- **What the app's own CSP needs** (`frame-src`, `script-src` and `connect-src` the frames' folder for host mode's Shiki and Temml, `frame-ancestors 'none'`), as a documented snippet, not something the plugin writes.
- **Never in a capability:** no page on the scheme reaches a Tauri command; a test shows it.
- **The example app and its self-check** (the next tasks), and how the build of the frames is wired (a `build.rs` step or a script before `tauri build`).
